title: Bellwether Logistics VPC capacity and Terraform upgrade playbook (initial draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This working draft collects the proposed VPC/on-prem sizing, Terraform module notes, and an upgrade/migration playbook for Bellwether Logistics' private deployment. Goal is to capture: recommended compute & network sizing for initial GA rollout, Terraform changes needed for the 2.1 runtime upgrade, a step-by-step migration plan with rollback points, and answers to the architecture Q&A we've been discussing with their infra team.

Audience: eng-private-deployments, infra SME, Bellwether infra and security leads, solutions engineering.

Status: initial draft. Highlights require validation with Bellwether network team (subnet CIDR availability) and their procurement timeline for GPUs.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Proposed baseline: 3 inference nodes with 8x A100-80GB equivalents in a private VPC (on-prem cage or dedicated cloud VPC) + 2 control-plane VMs (manager + metrics/ops). Estimated QPS headroom for 50k monthly active users with bursty peaks (~120 r/s).
- Terraform changes: introduce a new module bellwether-inference-cluster that composes node pool, kms-integration, and vpc-peering submodules. Use feature-flagged provider pinning to allow blue/green module upgrades.
- Upgrade approach: staged rollout across two AZs, canary traffic to new runtime image, automated data-plane backward-compatibility checks, final cutover with 15 minute rollback window.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Bellwether expects 99.5% availability SLA for business-critical routes.
- Average request token length forecast: 120 tokens; 40% of requests are 1–3 turn chat sessions.
- On-prem rack for inference supports NVLink and has 3 available 4U GPU servers (power/PDU adequate). If procurement is required, lead time ~6–8 weeks.
- Bellwether will provide peering VPN and at least two routable subnets (10.20.0.0/24 and 10.20.1.0/24) for control plane and data plane.

Sizing rationale and numbers (baseline):
- Workload profile: mixed chat + embeddings + reranking. Token/sec estimate per node (8xA100-80GB): ~5k tokens/s sustained with batching and KV cache.
- Baseline cluster: 3 inference nodes (worker role) to allow rolling upgrades and one node spare under typical load. Expected steady-state throughput ~15k tokens/s aggregate.
- Control plane: 2 m5a.large equivalent VMs for management, scheduler, and local metrics ingestion.
- Disk: 2TB NVMe per inference node for runtime swap, model artifacts and local KV cache persistence. PVs backed by local NVMe; backup snapshots to S3-compatible object store nightly.
- Network: 25 Gbps NICs recommended between inference nodes; MTU 9000 if Bellwether's switch fabric supports it.

Cost and procurement notes (rough, for Bellwether finance):
- On-prem capital: three 4U GPU servers w/ 8 x A100 equiv: estimate provided separately by solutions engineering.
- Operating: expected electricity and cooling footprint noted in the attachments (TODO: attach thermal profile).

Terraform module design notes (developer-facing):
- New module: modules/bellwether-inference-cluster
  - Inputs: cluster_name, env, vpc_id, subnets, kms_key_arn, allowed_cidrs, gpu_profile, node_count, storage_size_gb
  - Outputs: node_asg_ids, vpc_peering_id, kms_policy_id, cluster_tags
- Submodules: vpc-peering (reusable), kms-integration (wraps existing kms module + adds role trust relationship for Bellwether audit account), k8s-node-profile (cloud agnostic node pool config).
- Backwards compatibility: keep old module modules/inference-cluster-v1 for at least two release cycles. New module should be feature-flagged with variable enable_new_runtime (default false).
- State management: use remote state with locking (consul / s3+Dynamo lock). Plan files should be saved to artifact bucket with timestamped id.
- Breaking change handling: any API or naming change to IAM roles must be gated behind a controlled deploy ticket and a small IAM-only rollout to Bellwether's sandbox account.

Upgrade plan: 2.1 runtime upgrade (high-level steps)
1) Prep and validation (T-7 days):
   - Create feature branch for tf modules and bump runtime image tag.
   - Run static checks and terraform plan in Bellwether sandbox account.
   - Smoke deploy to staging cluster, perf tests run via existing harness (JMeter scripts).
2) Canary (T-2 days):
   - Deploy new runtime on 1 node in AZ-a; direct 5% of production traffic using traffic router. Run QA prompts suite and metrics regression checks.
   - Validate latency P95 and token-level cost delta (must be <= +7% or require signoff).
3) Progressive rollout (T+0):
   - If canary passes, roll new runtime to remaining nodes in AZ-a, then AZ-b. Monitor error rates and resource utilization.
   - Maintain live KV cache compatibility by running read-fallback to old runtime for 10 minutes after each node's cutover.
4) Finalization and cleanup (T+1 day):
   - Archive old images and increment module version. Update documentation and runbook.

Rollback criteria and plan:
- Stop rollout and rollback node to previous image if: error rate > 0.5% above baseline for 10m, or P95 latency increases > 20%, or token-cost delta > 12% and root cause unknown.
- Rollback steps: use TF to set enable_new_runtime=false, deploy old image to canary node, then sequentially to others. Expected recovery time 12–18 minutes per node depending on model load.

Network and security checklist (reqs to confirm with Bellwether):
- Confirm subnet CIDRs and available IP space; avoid 10.20.2.0/24 collision with partner network.
- Ensure eBPF firewall rules allowed between node-to-node telemetry ports (8000–8020).
- Confirm KMS policies for model key: we will need kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt and IAM role trust for redwood-deploy-user.
- TLS termination: Bellwether prefers internal LB TLS termination; provide cert rotation playbook.

Architecture Q&A (notes from recent call + proposed answers):
Q: How do we avoid model-version mismatch during rollout?
A: We will use model pins in cluster config and a staged data-plane flag. Model registry tag "bellwether-stable" will be updated only after canary passes. Runtime supports dual-read for cache warmup.

Q: Can we support air-gapped updates?
A: Yes. Provide OCI image tarballs and signed checksums. The tf module has a variable image_bundle_path for local registry imports.

Q: What about disaster recovery (DR)?
A: For on-prem primary with cloud backup, we recommend nightly object-store sync + weekly full backup and a warm standby region in the cloud running min-size cluster (1 node) to restore within 6 hours for critical routes. DR runbooks included in annex.

Open questions / action items (todo list):
- [ ] Confirm exact GPU SKU and vendor so we can tune nvlink + NUMA settings (owner: Liam; due: 2024-11-15)
- [ ] Bellwether to provide CIDR blocks and route table approval (owner: Bellwether infra)
- [ ] Security review on KMS trust policy (owner: Marina)
- [ ] Attach thermal and power profile from solutions engineering (owner: Sofia)

Testing and validation checklist (pre-cutover):
- Unit perf: run 20 min steady-state throughput test at 70% expected production.
- Regression evals: run curated prompt set (2000 prompts) and compare ROUGE/semantic diffs to baseline.
- Failover test: simulate node loss and check autoscaler behavior and request fallbacks.

Notes on operator ergonomics and observability: 
- Metric keys to monitor: tokens_per_sec, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_load_time, p95_latency_gen. Alerting thresholds suggested in annex.
- Console: add a Bellwether-specific dashboard with per-route latency + per-model cost breakdown.

Appendix A: Terraform snippet recommendations (examples)
- Example: gating the new runtime
  variable "enable_new_runtime" {
    type = bool
    default = false
  }

  resource "aws_launch_template" "inference" {
    name_prefix = "${var.cluster_name}-lt-"
    image_id    = var.enable_new_runtime ? data.aws_ami.new_runtime.id : data.aws_ami.old_runtime.id
  }

- Example: remote state lock (S3 + DynamoDB) and plan artifact upload hooks in CI.

Appendix B: Runbook quick commands (ops)
- Rollforward canary: terraform apply -var="enable_new_runtime=true" -target=module.bellwether-inference-cluster.aws_autoscaling_group.canary
- Force rollback: terraform apply -var="enable_new_runtime=false"

Annex: Links and artifacts (recorded for handoff)
- JMeter perf scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/perf/jmeter/bellwether_suite
- Eval prompt set: s3://redwood-evals/bellwether/initial_2000_set.json

Next steps and owners:
- Share this draft with Bellwether infra + security for validation (Sofia, 2024-11-09).
- Schedule a deep-dive on network peering details and cert rotation (Liam, 2024-11-12).
- Lock in procurement lead time and finalize SKU selection (Ethan, 2024-11-15).

Working notes / stray thoughts (scratch area):
- Might consider enabling a lightweight qps-based autoscaler for night windows to save OPEX; needs testing with warm-up penalties.
- Consider snapshotting KV caches pre-upgrade to speed warmup; requires checkpointing support in runtime.

Draft history: created by Sofia Alvarez 2024-11-07. Updated 2024-11-20 with Terraform module naming conventions and added canary thresholds per SRE review.
